sentences.text: This pterosaur had an estimated wingspan ranging from 1.8 to 1.9 meters.
Its upper jaws combined held approximately thirty-six teeth.
These teeth were robust and featured triangular crowns flattened from the mouth side to the lip side.
The species Hongshanopterus lacustris was named and described in 2008 by Wang Xiaolin, Diogenes de Almeida Campos, Zhou Zhonghe, and Alexander Wilhelm Armin Kellner.
Anatomy suggests a specialized feeding mechanism, as the pterosaur possessed a ridge on the underside of its pterygoid bone that pointed obliquely to the front and outside.
In 2008, Hongshanopterus was placed in the family Istiodactylidae in a basal position.
Hongshanopterus is classified in the family Istiodactylidae, though this classification is sometimes questioned.
Hongshanopterus lived in the Lower Cretaceous Jiufotang Formation of Liaoning, China.
It lived during the Aptian stage, between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
